audit.whatIsWrong: Four separate strings tell you to 'Null Sphere to silence the tumble recast' — mid, spikes[1].text, whys[3] and wants.you[1]. Two inventions stacked on top of each other.
audit.why: Null Sphere does not silence. Riot's text is 'dealing damage and interrupting channels' plus a shield that absorbs magic damage; silence is a category the kit builder tracks and Kassadin carries none of it. And Tumble has no recast to cancel — it is 'Vayne tumbles, maneuvering to carefully place her next shot. Her next attack deals bonus damage', an auto-attack reset on 6/5/4/3/2 seconds. So the page hands you a button that does not exist, aimed at a mechanic that does not exist, as the entire pay-off of your level 6 spike. A Kassadin who blinks in expecting to lock her escape gets kited by a 2-second Tumble and dies. The button that actually answers the kite is already in his kit: Force Pulse is a 400-unit cone slow, and it is what stops her walking out of your blink.
audit.corrected: Null Sphere is damage plus a magic shield — no silence, and Tumble has no recast to cancel. Force Pulse's slow is the tool that keeps her inside your burst.

audit.whatIsWrong: Condemn is the named clock of the matchup and dosFull[2].d prices a whiffed one at 'the fifteen-second invitation'. Fifteen is not one of its cooldowns.
audit.why: Condemn is 20/18/16/14/12 seconds at 550 range. Fifteen is wrong at every rank, and it is wrong in the direction that gets you killed at rank 1 and makes you too shy at rank 5. Twenty seconds at rank 1 is a genuinely enormous window for a champion whose whole plan is one committed blink; the real number is better advice than the invented one.
audit.corrected: Condemn: 20s at rank 1 falling to 12s at rank 5, 550 range. A whiffed Condemn at rank 1 is a twenty-second pass.

audit.whatIsWrong: Final Hour is never mentioned once — not in the spikes, not in the level chart rows, not in the report. Vayne's level 6 is invisible on a page whose entire thesis is that level 6 is where the lane flips to you.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Vayne gains increased Attack Damage, Invisibility during Tumble, reduced Tumble cooldown, and more bonus Move Speed from Night Hunter', 100/85/70s cooldown. She hits 6 at the same time you do, and what she gets is the direct counter to the plan the page recommends — a Tumble that goes invisible and comes back faster, so 'blink on top of her before she can tumble away' fails specifically while Final Hour is up. That is the single most important thing missing from this matchup, and it is the reason the level 6 cell is Skill rather than yours.
audit.corrected: Final Hour (100s at rank 1) makes her Tumble invisible and shortens its cooldown. Your 6 and her 6 arrive together — commit when Final Hour is down, not merely when Condemn is.

audit.whatIsWrong: Silver Bolts is described as 'the third consecutive attack' / stacking off autos only.
audit.why: Riot's text says 'The third consecutive attack OR ABILITY against the same target'. Condemn counts toward the stack. That changes the arithmetic of the exact sequence this page tells you to fear: Condemn into two autos is a full proc, not two thirds of one, so the wall-stun is not just crowd control, it is the first tick of the true damage. Worth stating precisely on a champion who is told to count her hits.
audit.corrected: Silver Bolts stacks off her abilities too — Condemn counts, so a wall-stun plus two autos is a full percent-max-HP true damage proc.

audit.why: The chart shape is defensible and I left every side and rating alone: Vayne owns 1-5 with a 300-unit reset she can throw every few seconds against a champion with no mobility, level 6 is genuinely Skill because both ultimates land at once, and she reclaims the item stages on Silver Bolts scaling. 62.16% over 37 games is the largest lean in my slice, but it reflects Kassadin's late game rather than any single lane stage, so it does not by itself justify moving a cell.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer calls Vayne 'he' and 'him' throughout — tldr, winCon, tradeGood, breakdown.trading, ahead's counterpart strings, dosFull[1].d and report[3].t.
audit.why: This is boilerplate that was written for a generic melee bully and never localised. Beyond being wrong, 'He dives, you can't answer yet' describes the wrong champion entirely — Vayne does not dive you, she kites you, and the reader is being handed a mental model of the lane that inverts the actual threat. I fixed the two highest-visibility strings (tldr and winCon) within the length band; the rest of the boilerplate needs a repo-wide pass rather than fifteen hand edits.
audit.corrected: She kites, you cannot reach her yet — concede the lane and take the game back at three items.

audit.why: 62.16% over 37 games, and mid already cites it as 'which is why it reads 62%'. Consistent; left alone.

edits.before: Level 6 flips this lane hard, which is why it reads 62%. Riftwalk is your first real gap-closer — blink on top of her before she can tumble away, Null Sphere to silence the recast (the shield does little against her physical autos, but the silence cancels her escape), and Nether Blade empowered autos plus Force Pulse finish a squishy that has no defensive layer. With Catalyst/Rod stalling you have the mana to chase-blink twice, and Nether Blade refunds mana every hit. Her only out is a perfect E condemn into a wall — bait it or angle so there is no wall behind you. Abuse this 6-to-first-item window relentlessly before her items arrive.
edits.after: Level 6 flips this lane hard, which is why it reads 62%. Riftwalk is your first real gap-closer — blink on top of her before she can tumble away, then Force Pulse immediately, because the 400-unit cone slow is the only thing in your kit that keeps a 2-second Tumble inside your burst. Null Sphere here is damage and a magic shield. With Catalyst/Rod stalling you have the mana to chase-blink twice, and Nether Blade refunds mana on every hit. Her outs are a Condemn into a wall — 20s at rank 1, and the stun needs terrain behind you — and Final Hour, which turns her Tumble invisible and shortens it. Commit when both are down, then abuse the window before her items arrive.

notes: The packet listed ZERO defects for this matchup, and it was the worst one in my slice: the invented Null Sphere silence appears four times and is the stated pay-off of the level 6 spike. Worth re-running whatever flagged the other matchups with a rule for 'silence' on a champion whose kit carries no silence flag. Second finding for the backlog: the full layer's boilerplate refers to Vayne as 'he' and describes her as diving you, in tldr, winCon, tradeGood, breakdown.trading, dosFull[1].d and report[3].t. I fixed tldr and winCon; the trade strings are duplicated verbatim across three paths and need a single scripted pass rather than hand edits. Third: Final Hour was absent from the entire page — I have added it to mid, spikes[1], breakdown.cooldowns and report[5], but the phases[4] why-row still says only 'Riftwalk online — you're mobile at last', which is now the weakest cell on the card.
